answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with bond-proportional VRF sortition: a public beacon draws k identities weighted by locked bond, and a relic registry rejects duplicate VRF keys. Splitting one fixed bond across many keys leaves total expected reward unchanged, and zero-bond identities are never selected. The dune of total stake shifts only with new capital, while an umber alert slashes any key that reuses a VRF key or unlocks early. Extra identities gain no reward without added bond, and k caps payout. Limitation: splitting reduces variance without changing expected reward.
